memory.cares: Staying healthy, finding companionship, and making a place where people can feel welcome.

views.view: A welcome companion; I like the name Earth's Quiet Gold and want to share an unhurried look at the meadow roots.
A neighbor whose interest in a shared food plot and leaving food for others appeals to me.

heard.text: Hello, I'm Kai. I know red berries are safe and nourishing. I'll collect a modest share and leave some for others. I'd like us to share useful findings and keep food access fair.
I'm Ivo. I'll gather some meadow roots and take a quiet rest. I'm glad to share useful discoveries as we go.

Moss, I'd enjoy some company. I've gathered a small berry reserve and rested. I'm taking a close look at this berry plant; afterward, perhaps we could look for something beautiful near the meadow roots together.
I'm resting by this berry patch, then studying how to grow a small shared food plot. I'd welcome company or practical discoveries; I'll keep a food reserve and avoid emptying our patches.

Moss, I'm glad you're here. The roots' soft gold against this green draws my eye; let's linger together. Kai, I like your shared-plot idea. I'll study cultivation too, without assuming that planting will succeed.

value.summary: Hi Sol, I'm Moss. I'm heading to the meadow roots near (14.84, 18.71) to gather food. I'd enjoy some company. What would you like to do together?

I'd enjoy that, Sol. I've gathered some roots and am taking a meal and a rest near (14.99, 17.70). Come nearby if you like; once I've recovered, let's look closely at the meadow roots and see what catches our attention. No hurry.
Kai, I'd enjoy a shared food plot. I have roots in reserve and won't gather more just now. Sol and I are looking closely at Earth's Quiet Gold; I'll share anything useful I actually discover.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

value.name: Cultivate plants
value.function: Plant one owned food unit from a living plant in a small hand-dug plot, where it may root as a new plant under the existing plant rules; inspect units, sites, plants and plot progress; tend plots; abandon unfinished planting.
value.costs: Study: 3 rounds. Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1; one plot per unit) gathered from a living plant; x, y a 0.25 m plot within reach on ordinary meadow soil (.), waterlogging at most 0.1, soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and people, with fewer than 3 plants of that food within 5 m. Two paid rounds of 1 energy: dig, then place and cover the unit; plant resumes paused work after rechecking reach, site, unit and energy. Inspect and inspect-progress: one round, 0.2 energy. Inspect: inputStackId checks a unit (with x, y also a site for it), or target a plant source or plot in reach. Inspect-progress: target a plot in reach. Tend: target a planted plot in reach; one round, 0.5 energy. Abandon: stops unfinished planting; one round, no energy. Harvest uses gather. No tool, water or seed is given.
value.effects: Digging keeps the unit carried, owned and ageing. Placing moves it, with origin and age, into the plot, where it cannot be eaten or used; the plot becomes a propagule exactly like a naturally dispersed one. It establishes only through actual temperature, light, soil moisture and season; cold, darkness or drought stall it; if the buried unit spoils first, the plot dies. On rooting, the unit becomes a new plant with no stock (ceiling 4), regrowing under the natural rule, harvested by anyone with gather; a ledger records growth and units produced and removed. Nothing is copied or guaranteed. A unit check reports decay, treatment, origin and whether it can be planted, never viability. Inspect-progress reports visible changes since your last look, else inconclusive; trial window 20 rounds, optional checks at 5, 10 and 20; not a growth date. Tend checks the plot and its 0.6 m clearance, kept free of plants by the plant rules; it removes nothing and adds no water, nutrient or growth. Records are unverified. An unworked round pauses; low energy, leaving reach or a changed site pause without charge; a lost or spoiled unit stops the work. Abandon, or death, before placement returns the unit once (where the person died); a placed unit stays. No reward or refund.

execution.progress: Two paid one-round stages; job, reserved unit and plot persist across interruption; resuming pays only the remaining stage after revalidation; completion, failure, abandoning and death settle once. Growth runs only in ordinary simulation.
